x: The highest forest loss is concentrated in tropical forests, especially in the Amazon, Congo Basin and Southeast Asia.

s: As per FAO FRA 2025, which is the only region with a net gain in forest area?
x: Asia, led by China and India, is the only region with a net forest gain.

s: As per FAO FRA 2025, what was the annual net forest loss during 2015-2025?
x: FRA 2025 puts net loss at 10.7 Mha/yr in the 1990s falling to 4.12 Mha/yr in 2015-2025; 8.3 to 5.2 is the older FRA.

s: As per FAO FRA 2025, what is India's rank in the world in forest area?
x: India is 9th in forest area (10th in 2020) and 3rd in annual forest gain.

s: As per the India State of Forest Report 2023, what share of India's area is under forest and tree cover?
x: Forest plus tree cover is 25.17% (forest 21.76%, tree 3.41%).

s: As per ISFR 2023, which State recorded the largest loss of forest cover?
x: Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka had the largest losses; Chhattisgarh, UP and Odisha were among the top gainers.

s: As per ISFR 2023, which State recorded the highest gain in forest and tree cover?
x: Chhattisgarh led the gains, followed by Uttar Pradesh, Odisha and Rajasthan.

s: As per FAO FRA 2025, what is India's rank in the world in annual gain in forest area?
x: FRA 2025 ranks India 9th in forest area and 3rd in annual gain of forest area.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the extent of land degradation?
o: The 2021 Atlas reports about 97.85 Mha of India as degraded
About 29.77% of India's area is degraded as per the 2021 Atlas
According to FAO, about one-half of the world's soils are degraded
Water erosion and chemical degradation are major contributors in India
x: FAO says about one-third, not one-half, of the world's soils are degraded.

s: The Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas was published by which organisation and centre?
o: Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education, Dehradun
National Atlas and Thematic Mapping Organisation, Kolkata
x: The Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas was published by ISRO's Space Applications Centre located at Ahmedabad.

s: About what share of India's degraded land faces desertification?
x: About one-fourth of degraded land faces desertification; Rajasthan accounts for more than 23% of India's desertified land.

s: Which two regions are identified as the worst-hit continents or zones in terms of desertification?
o: Africa, particularly the Sahel, and Asia
x: Africa, especially the Sahel region, and Asia are identified as the worst-hit regions in relation to desertification.

s: Which State has over 23% of India's desertified land?
x: Rajasthan has over 23% of India's desertified land.

s: As per the Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas 2021, what share of India's area is degraded?
x: About 97.85 Mha, or 29.77% of India, is degraded; 33.81% is Andhra Pradesh's figure.

s: As per the Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas 2021, which are the main contributors to land degradation in India?
o: Waterlogging and wind erosion of dunes
x: The Atlas identifies water erosion and chemical degradation as the main contributors.

s: Which Indian region is notably affected by sand and dust storms?
x: Sand and dust storms hit NW India (Rajasthan), West Asia and the Sahel.

s: In which season are dust storms most common in north-west India?
x: Dust storms in Rajasthan and north-west India are most common in the hot, dry pre-monsoon summer months (April to June).

s: At UNCCD COP14 in New Delhi (2019), India raised its land-restoration target to how much by 2030?
x: At COP14 India raised its target to 26 Mha by 2030, up from the 21 Mha pledged at Paris in 2015.

s: Where was UNCCD COP17 held, at which India's first guide to Grasslands and Open Natural Ecosystems was launched?
x: COP17 (2026) was held at Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia; New Delhi hosted COP14 in 2019.

s: On which date is the World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought observed?
x: The World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought is observed on 17 June, following a 1994 UNGA decision.

s: On which date is the international day linked to the UN Decade on Combating Sand and Dust Storms (2025-2034) observed?
x: The related day is observed on 12 July; the UNGA declared 2025–2034 the UN Decade on Combating Sand and Dust Storms.

s: What was India's land-restoration target set at Paris in 2015, before COP14?
x: India raised its target from 21 Mha (Paris 2015) to 26 Mha by 2030 at COP14, New Delhi.

s:
Consider the following statements about the UNCCD:
1. It is the only legally binding framework on desertification.
2. It is one of the three Rio conventions.
3. India ratified it in 1994.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; India ratified the UNCCD in 1996, the year it entered into force.

s: What is the full form of UNCCD?
o: United Nations Commission on Climate and Development
United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification
United Nations Convention on Climate Change and Drought
United Nations Council for Combating Desertification
x: UNCCD stands for the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification, adopted in Paris in 1994.

s: Where is the secretariat of the UNCCD located?
x: The UNCCD was adopted in Paris in 1994, but its secretariat is in Bonn, Germany.

s: The Global Land Outlook is the flagship publication of which body?
x: The Global Land Outlook (2017, 2022) is the flagship report of the UNCCD.

s: Which country hosted the World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought in 2026?
x: Kenya hosted the 2026 Day (17 June) on the theme 'Rangelands: Recognise. Respect. Restore.'

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the UNCCD?
o: It was adopted in 1994 in Paris
Its secretariat is located in Bonn
India is a party to the Convention
x: The UNCCD was adopted in Paris in 1994 but entered into force only in 1996; its secretariat is in Bonn and India is a party.

s: The Bonn Challenge was launched in 2011 by which of the following?
x: The Bonn Challenge was launched in 2011 by Germany and the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India and the Bonn Challenge?
o: India joined at Paris in 2015 with a pledge of 21 million hectares
Telangana led the States with about 4.18 million hectares restored
India restored about 21.76 million hectares during 2011-2020
Andhra Pradesh led all States in land restored during 2011-2020
x: Per the MoEFCC-IUCN report Telangana led (4.18 Mha), followed by MP, Odisha, Gujarat and then Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about land-restoration initiatives?
o: The Aravalli Green Wall aims to check the eastward spread of the Thar
The Great Green Wall is an African Union-led belt across the Sahel
The Bonn Challenge targets 150 Mha by 2020 and 350 Mha by 2030
The Bonn Challenge is an African Union-led belt across the Sahel
x: The Sahelian belt is the Great Green Wall of Africa; the Bonn Challenge is defined by its 150 Mha (2020) and 350 Mha (2030) restoration targets.

s: On 24 December 2025, MoEFCC announced which measure for the Aravallis?
o: Declaration of the range as a tiger reserve
A ban on all construction activity
Cancellation of all existing mining leases
A ban on granting any new mining leases
x: On 24 December 2025, MoEFCC banned the grant of any new mining leases in the Aravallis.

s: SPSR Nellore has set a target of achieving what level of green cover by 2047?
x: SPSR Nellore targets 50% green cover by 2047 (Jul 2026) under the Great Green Wall of Andhra Pradesh, which aims to raise green cover and combat desertification.

s: Who launched the Great Green Wall across Africa's Sahel belt?
x: The Great Green Wall is led by the African Union; the Bonn Challenge was launched by Germany and IUCN.

s: The Bonn Challenge aims to restore how much degraded land by 2030?
x: The Bonn Challenge targets 150 Mha by 2020 and 350 Mha by 2030.

s: Which of the following is NOT covered by the Aravalli Green Wall project?
x: The Aravalli Green Wall covers Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana and Delhi as a barrier to the Thar; Madhya Pradesh is not included.

s: As per MoEFCC-IUCN, which State led India's land restoration during 2011-2020?
x: India restored 21.76 Mha in 2011-2020; Telangana led with 4.18 Mha, followed by MP, Odisha, Gujarat and AP.

s: The Great Green Wall of Africa aims to restore how much land by 2030?
x: The African Union's Great Green Wall across the Sahel, from Senegal to Djibouti, targets 100 million ha by 2030.

s: What is the removal of a thin, even layer of topsoil over a wide area called?
x: Sheet erosion removes a thin even layer of topsoil; rills are small channels and gullies deep channels.

s: What are the deep gully channels of the Chambal basin known as?
x: Gully erosion in clayey soil creates badlands, called ravines in the Chambal basin.

s: Which of the following pairs (conservation method – how it works) is correctly matched?
o: Strip cropping – steps cut on slopes
Shelter belts – grass strips between crops
Contour ploughing – ploughing along contours slows water down slopes
x: Contour ploughing slows water down slopes; terracing cuts steps, strip cropping uses grass strips and shelter belts are tree windbreaks.

s: Shelter belts have helped stabilise sand dunes in which part of India?
x: Shelter belts are tree rows used as windbreaks; they stabilised dunes in western India.

s: Where was the Soil Health Card scheme launched on 19 February 2015?
x: The Soil Health Card scheme was launched at Suratgarh, Rajasthan, on 19 February 2015.

s: How often is a Soil Health Card issued to farmers?
x: A Soil Health Card is issued every 2 years.

s: Which soil-conservation method grows strips of grass between crops to break the force of wind?
x: Strip cropping leaves strips of grass between crops to break wind force; shelter belts use rows of trees.

s: The Namo Van–Nagar Van Scheme primarily seeks to achieve which of the following?
o: Replacement of all rural forests with plantations
Expansion of mining areas around cities
Reduction of the urban heat island effect through urban forests
x: The Namo Van–Nagar Van Scheme promotes urban forests with the aim of reducing the urban heat island effect.

s: Which of the following contributes to the formation of urban heat islands?
x: Loss of vegetation is a cause of urban heat islands, alongside heat-storing low-albedo concrete and asphalt; cool roofs and urban forests counter them.

s: Which of the following best describes a cool roof?
o: A roof designed to store solar heat for night-time use
A roof made only of metallic sheets
A roof treated with a high-reflectance coating to reduce heat absorption
A roof covered entirely with vegetation
x: Cool roofs use white or reflective, high-reflectance coatings that reduce heat absorption and lower the indoor cooling load.

s: Which one of the following is NOT an objective of the Andhra Pradesh Cool Surface Policy, 2023?
o: Promoting the use of reflective materials
Promoting rural heat as a separate policy objective
Providing affordable solutions against urban heat
x: The policy objectives include affordable urban heat solutions, reduction of heat and energy demand, and promotion of reflective materials. Rural heat is not identified as an objective.

s: India's first Heat Action Plan was prepared by which city in 2013?
x: Ahmedabad prepared India's first Heat Action Plan in 2013.

s: In which year did the NDMA issue its heat action plan guidelines?
x: The NDMA issued heat action plan guidelines in 2016, after Ahmedabad's first plan in 2013.

s: As per the SDG India Index 2023-24, what share of Andhra Pradesh's land is degraded?
x: Under SDG 15 (SDG India Index 2023-24), degraded land is 33.81% of AP, about ten times Punjab's 3.15%. 18.28% is AP's forest cover and 21.26% its fallow-land share.

s: In Andhra Pradesh, which districts are most associated with drought-induced land degradation, wind erosion of topsoil and groundwater depletion?
o: Anantapur and Sri Sathya Sai districts
Uppada and the Krishna delta only
x: Anantapur and Sri Sathya Sai are associated with drought-induced degradation, desertification, wind erosion of topsoil and groundwater depletion.

s: Which of the following regional pairs is correctly matched?
x: Uppada in Kakinada is associated with coastal erosion. Delta areas are associated with salinity and waterlogging.

s: Which measures are used against desertification in Rayalaseema?
x: Rayalaseema relies on ridge-to-valley watershed works, afforestation and green-wall planting; straw checkerboards belong to China's Three-North programme.

s: As per the SDG India Index 2023-24, which State has the least degraded land?
x: Punjab has the least degraded land at 3.15%, against Andhra Pradesh's 33.81%.

s: What share of Andhra Pradesh's area is fallow land, which exceeds its forest area?
x: AP's fallow land is 21.26% (34.65 lakh ha), more than its forest cover of 18.28%.

s: What share of the area of Andhra Pradesh is under forest cover?
x: Andhra Pradesh has 18.28% forest cover and 2.87% tree cover; its fallow land (21.26%) is more than its forest area.
